newsitem.title: UK: Shell gains after ADR strength.
newsitem.headline: Shell gains after ADR strength.

text.p: Shares in Shell Transport & Trading Co Plc rose on Wednesday, echoing strength on Wall Street in the ADRs of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, dealers said.

Shell shares were up 11-1/2p at 10.40-1/2 stg by 1027 GMT in moderate trade of 1.5 million shares, rebounding from their three-month closing low of 10.26 stg set April 14. "They are just rebounding having been sold off a bit too harshly," said one senior dealer.
In the U.S., Royal Dutch ADRs rose $2-5/8 to $172-5/8.

Dealers said there was also vague market talk that Shell and Unilever Plc -- both with listings in Britain and the Netherlands -- could raise their sterling dividends to offset any reduction in the dividend tax credit for tax-exempt funds by an incoming Labour government after the May 1 election.
The aim would be to equalise the value of the sterling and guilder dividends.

"Shell and Unilever are benefitting from hopes for a dividend boost if there is any change in the tax credit," said one dealer. "There is talk that it will have to raise the sterling dividend to offset any tax hit."

A research note from BZW said Labour might seek to raise five billion stg through higher corporate taxes, though the brokerage said a move on advance corporation tax (ACT) in isolation was less likely than a general review of company taxes.
Under the current system, tax-exempt pension funds can reclaim the ACT that companies pay on their dividends.
However, others remained sceptical that Shell would change its dividend policy in response to any ACT move by Labour.
"Shell has shown disdain towards some of the ideas put to the company by its followers," said one analyst.
